svg.desc: Two panels over the first 30 people of Bikhchandani, Hirshleifer and Welch's binary example, in which each person sees only the actions of those before her, for signal precisions 0.6 (orange) and 0.75 (dark). Top, the probability that a cascade has started, solid, and that a wrong cascade has started, dashed: the probability of no cascade after 10 people is 0.00080 and 0.00023, and that of a wrong cascade levels off at 0.368 and 0.192. Bottom, the bits about the gain from adopting, which starts at one bit of uncertainty: in the actions of those who have acted, solid, levelling off at 0.051 and 0.294, and in the same people's private signals, dashed, 0.554 and 0.993 after 30 people. One signal carries 0.029 and 0.189 bits, and the public history of a cascade is worth 1.33 and 1.31 private signals in log-odds. Every number is this book's calculation.
